subject: Career
title: SEO for People: Being Findable
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on SEO for People: Being Findable.

hook.text: A recruiter searches 'data scientist healthcare Python.' Your profile needs to match those words.

buildup.text: Just like websites, professional profiles rank based on keyword relevance and activity.

discovery.text: Using industry-specific terms in your headline, summary, and skills makes you discoverable.

twist.text: Keyword stuffing backfires. Natural language with strategic terms works best.

climax.text: Think like your ideal employer. What would they search? Put those words on your profile.

punchline.text: You can't be hired if you can't be found.

quiz.question: How does SEO thinking apply to professional profiles?
options: Using industry keywords makes profiles discoverable to recruiters
Adding every possible skill helps most

details.summary: Personal SEO means optimizing your online presence so that you appear prominently when people search for your name or your area of expertise. It involves keyword-rich profiles, consistent naming, and regular content creation on indexed platforms.
details.whyItMatters: If someone searches your name and finds nothing or finds the wrong person, you lose credibility and opportunities. Being findable and correctly represented online is a baseline professional requirement.
takeaways: Use your full name consistently across all professional platforms
Include relevant industry keywords in your LinkedIn and website copy
Regular content creation on indexed platforms pushes you higher in search

faq.question: What is the fastest way to improve your personal search results?
faq.answer: Create profiles on high-authority sites like LinkedIn, Medium, and relevant industry platforms using your full name. Publish two to three pieces of content with your name attached. These high-authority platforms rank quickly and push down irrelevant results.

faq.question: What if you share a name with someone more famous?
faq.answer: Add a middle initial, professional suffix, or descriptor to differentiate yourself. Use 'Jane M. Smith, Data Strategist' consistently across platforms. Creating a personal website with your name as the domain also helps you claim search real estate.
